note: Chiu et al. (2026) reported sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges in 4/5 (80%) and hippocampal sclerosis in 3/5 (60%) patients with dominant RNU2-2 DEE, directly supporting the proposed signature.

evidence.text: In individuals with RNU2-2 DEE, electroencephalography showed sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges in 4 of 5 patients, and brain magnetic resonance imaging showed hippocampal sclerosis in 3 of 5 patients.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Electroencephalography showed sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges (n = 4) and hippocampal sclerosis on magnetic resonance imaging (n = 3).

evidence.text: De novo variants in snRNA genes RNU4-2 (ReNU syndrome) and RNU2-2 cause neurodevelopmental disorders and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies with overlapping yet distinctive genetic and phenotypic presentations.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: De novo variants in snRNA genes RNU4-2 (ReNU syndrome), RNU5B-1 and RNU2-2 have been linked to dominant neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), revealing a large unexpected contribution of noncoding RNA genes to genetic diseases.
